---
title: Reference List — MIPSA Data Processing & Modelling
---

### Prioritised for the Task of "Improving MIPSA Reaction Estimates by Appropriate Modelling"


## Tier 1 — Directly Foundational to the Modelling Task

**Chen, A., et al. (2022)**
*Detecting and quantifying antibody reactivity in PhIP-Seq data with BEER.*
Bioinformatics, 38(19), 4647–4655.
https://academic.oup.com/bioinformatics/article/38/19/4647/6663763

The closest existing work to the proposed model. BEER implements a Bayesian hierarchical model for count-level probe aggregation in PhIP-Seq/MIPSA data, and explicitly addresses the sensitivity gap for weakly reactive peptides. Any new modelling framework should position itself clearly relative to BEER.

---

**Robinson, M. D., McCarthy, D. J., & Smyth, G. K. (2010)**
*edgeR: a Bioconductor package for differential expression analysis of digital gene expression data.*
Bioinformatics, 26(1), 139–140.

The current workhorse for MIPSA hit calling. The proposed model must benchmark against it. Understanding its negative binomial, empirical Bayes dispersion estimation framework is prerequisite knowledge.

---

**Irizarry, R. A., et al. (2003)**
*Exploration, normalization, and summaries of high density oligonucleotide array probe level data.*
Biostatistics, 4(2), 249–264.

The RMA paper — the direct methodological ancestor of the proposed model. Establishes the log-additive probe-aggregation framework and robust fitting approach that the MIPSA model adapts into the count / negative binomial setting.

---

## Tier 2 — Structurally Important, Directly Informative

**Credle, J. J., et al. (Larman lab) (2022)**
*Unbiased discovery of autoantibodies associated with severe COVID-19 via genome-scale self-assembled DNA-barcoded protein libraries.*
Nature Biomedical Engineering.
https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10034860/

The primary technical reference for MIPSA. Critical for understanding UCI structure in full-length ORFeome libraries, the role of mock IPs, and the existing informatic pipeline. The Methods section is essentially the starting specification for the modelling work.

---

**Infinity Bio (2024)**
*VirSIGHT MIPSA Report — Sample Report.*
https://www.infinitybio.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/07/Infinity-Bio_IB0000_VirSIGHT_Report-1.html

The most explicit operational description of the current data processing pipeline: Bowtie2 alignment, mock IP structure, edgeR hit calling, and QC metrics. The direct target for improvement in Phase 1.

---

## Tier 3 — Useful Context, Less Directly Actionable

**Galloway, J. G., et al. (2023)**
*Phippery — integrated processing of PhIP-Seq raw data.*
GitHub / Software release.

Relevant for Phase 2 (software packaging). Useful reference for what pipeline infrastructure already exists so the proposed R package does not duplicate it unnecessarily.

---

**Liebhoff, A-M., Venkataraman, T., Morgenlander, W. R., ..., Larman, H. B. (2024)**
*Efficient encoding of large antigenic spaces by epitope prioritization with Dolphyn.*
Nature Communications, 15, 1577.
https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-024-45601-8

Relevant to library design and peptide tile efficiency. The machine-learning-based tile selection approach in Dolphyn directly informs what drives probe-level efficiency differences (γ_i in the proposed model).

---

## Tier 4 — Background / Field Context

**Larman, H. B., et al. (2011)**
*Autoantigen discovery with a synthetic human peptidome.*
Nature Biotechnology, 29(6), 535–541.

The foundational PhIP-Seq paper. Establishes the peptide tiling and immunoprecipitation-sequencing paradigm that MIPSA builds on. Essential background for the manuscript introduction.

---

**Wang, E. Y., Rosen, C. E., et al. (2022)**
*High-throughput identification of autoantibodies that target the human exoproteome.*
Cell Reports Methods, 2(3), 100172.
https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8967185/

The foundational REAP paper. Relevant as a complementary technology to MIPSA with a distinct display mechanism and antigen scope. Useful for contextualising MIPSA's positioning in the manuscript.

---

**Frontiers in Bioinformatics (2024)**
*PhIP-Seq: methods, applications and challenges.*
https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/bioinformatics/articles/10.3389/fbinf.2024.1424202/full

and

**Molecular & Cellular Proteomics (2024)**
*Phage Immunoprecipitation and Sequencing — a Versatile Technique for Mapping the Antibody Reactome.*
https://www.mcponline.org/article/S1535-9476(24)00121-X/fulltext

Both useful for the manuscript introduction and for citing the acknowledged absence of a standardised, principled analysis pipeline — which directly motivates the proposed work.

---

## Note on the RMA Literature More Broadly

The broader normalisation literature from the early microarray era (Speed lab, ~2001–2005) provides useful methodological grounding, particularly on robust probe-level estimation and between-array normalisation. This is background rather than required citation, but worth keeping accessible.
